summary.one_liner: kro (Kube Resource Orchestrator) is a Kubernetes SIG Cloud Provider subproject that lets you group multiple Kubernetes resources into reusable custom resources defined by a ResourceGraphDefinition.
summary.what_it_does: kro provides a fundamental custom resource called ResourceGraphDefinition (RGD) that bundles one or more Kubernetes resources, native or custom, and specifies the dependencies between them. When an RGD is applied to a cluster running the kro controller, kro validates it, dynamically creates a new CRD and registers it with the API server, and deploys a dedicated controller to manage instances of that CRD. The controller works out dependency order to create and configure the underlying resources, then manages their lifecycle. The README's example is a WebApp RGD composed of a Deployment and a Service, which can be combined with a database resource into a larger WebAppWithDB group. The README describes the project's API as v1alpha1, with breaking changes possible.
use_cases: Define reusable custom resources composed of several Kubernetes objects
Package a web app's Deployment and Service as a single custom resource
Combine app resources with cloud-managed infrastructure such as a database
Manage resource creation order and dependencies automatically
Provide default configurations for complex Kubernetes resource groups
how_to_run: Install kro in your cluster (see the Installation docs linked in the README)
Apply a ResourceGraphDefinition to the cluster where the kro controller is running
Create an instance of the CRD that the ResourceGraphDefinition generates
notable: Uses a ResourceGraphDefinition CRD to define groups of resources and their dependencies
Dynamically generates a new CRD and a dedicated microcontroller per definition
Kubernetes-native and vendor agnostic, per the README
Resolves dependency ordering between resources automatically
caveats: API is at v1alpha1, so breaking changes may occur
README gives no detailed installation or run commands; it points to external docs
